Exercise 9.3 — The FOCOPS policy for two actions
      
      
        One state, two actions, $\pi_k=(\tfrac12,\tfrac12)$, advantages $A=(+1,-1)$ and cost advantages $A_c=(+2,-2)$ (both average to zero under $\pi_k$, as advantages must). Let $p=\pi^\star(a_1)$ in the closed form of Section 4. (a) Write $p$ as a function of the temperature $\lambda$ and the cost multiplier $\nu$. (b) With $\lambda=1$ and the cost constraint $\mathbb E_{\pi^\star}[A_c]\le\tilde b=0.5$, find the smallest feasible $\nu$ and the resulting $p$. (c) Compute $D_{\mathrm{KL}}(\pi^\star\|\pi_k)$ and compare it with $\delta=0.05$. What are the exact multipliers of the two-constraint problem? (d) Repeat for $\delta=0.02$: which constraint binds now?
        
          Show answer
          
            (a) $\pi^\star(a)\propto\pi_k(a)\exp\big((A(a)-\nu A_c(a))/\lambda\big)$, so with $u=(1-2\nu)/\lambda$: $p=\frac{e^{u}}{e^{u}+e^{-u}}=\sigma\big(2(1-2\nu)/\lambda\big)$, $\sigma$ the logistic function (see Primer E).
            (b) $\mathbb E_{\pi^\star}[A_c]=2p-2(1-p)=4p-2\le0.5\iff p\le0.625$. With $\nu=0$: $p=\sigma(2)\approx0.881$, violated. Equality: $2(1-2\nu)=\ln\frac{0.625}{0.375}=\ln\tfrac53\approx0.511$, so $\nu=\tfrac12-\tfrac14\ln\tfrac53\approx0.372$ and $p=0.625$. The objective is $\mathbb E_{\pi^\star}[A]=2p-1=0.25$, down from $2\sigma(2)-1\approx0.762$ without the cost constraint.
            (c) $D_{\mathrm{KL}}=0.625\ln1.25+0.375\ln0.75=\tfrac58\ln\tfrac54-\tfrac38\ln\tfrac43\approx0.0316\lt0.05$: the trust region is slack. The exact solution of the two-constraint problem is therefore $p=0.625$, with multipliers $(\lambda,\nu)=(0,\,0.5)$ by complementary slackness and stationarity of the (now linear) Lagrangian $2p-1-\nu(4p-2.5)$; the Gibbs form degenerates at $\lambda=0$. FOCOPS with the temperature fixed at $\lambda=1$ reaches the same policy with $\nu=\tfrac12-\tfrac14\ln\tfrac53\approx0.372$. With a single free parameter $p$, a fixed temperature reproduces it whenever an admissible $\nu\ge0$ makes the cost constraint tight: $p=0.625$ requires $\nu=\tfrac12-\tfrac\lambda4\ln\tfrac53$, which is non-negative only for $\lambda\le2/\ln\tfrac53\approx3.915$. For hotter temperatures the unconstrained Gibbs policy already has $p=\sigma(2/\lambda)\lt0.625$ (e.g. $p\approx0.583$ at $\lambda=6$), so $\nu=0$ and FOCOPS takes a smaller step than the exact solution. The multiplier values are not comparable across temperatures.
            (d) $D_{\mathrm{KL}}(p)=p\ln2p+(1-p)\ln2(1-p)$ increases for $p\gt\tfrac12$. Let $p^\star$ be its unique root $D_{\mathrm{KL}}(p^\star)=0.02$ in $[\tfrac12,\tfrac58]$; $0.59966520\lt p^\star\lt0.59966521$, so $p^\star\approx0.5997$ (check: $0.6\ln1.2+0.4\ln0.8\approx0.0201\gt0.02$). Now the KL constraint binds first: $4p^\star-2\approx0.399\lt0.5$ leaves the cost constraint slack, so $\nu^\star=0$, and the temperature solves $\sigma(2/\lambda^\star)=p^\star$, i.e. $2/\lambda^\star=\ln\frac{p^\star}{1-p^\star}\approx0.404$, $\lambda^\star=2/\ln\frac{p^\star}{1-p^\star}\approx4.95$. It indeed minimises the dual $\lambda\delta+\lambda\ln\cosh(1/\lambda)$: the derivative $\delta+\ln\cosh(1/\lambda)-\tanh(1/\lambda)/\lambda$ vanishes there. Moral: the two multipliers take turns; FOCOPS in practice fixes $\lambda$, adapts only $\nu$, and applies per-state KL rejection and sampled-average KL early stopping.
